author: tenderlove
body:
This commit inlines instructions for Class#new.  To make this work, we added a new YARV instructions, `opt_new`.  `opt_new` checks whether or not the `new` method is the default allocator method.  If it is, it allocates the object, and pushes the instance on the stack.  If not, the instruction jumps to the "slow path" method call instructions.

Old instructions:

```
> ruby --dump=insns -e'Object.new'
== disasm: #<ISeq:<main>@-e:1 (1,0)-(1,10)>
0000 opt_getconstant_path                   <ic:0 Object>             (   1)[Li]
0002 opt_send_without_block                 <calldata!mid:new, argc:0, ARGS_SIMPLE>
0004 leave
```

New instructions:

```
> ./miniruby --dump=insns -e'Object.new'
== disasm: #<ISeq:<main>@-e:1 (1,0)-(1,10)>
0000 opt_getconstant_path                   <ic:0 Object>             (   1)[Li]
0002 putnil
0003 swap
0004 opt_new                                <calldata!mid:new, argc:0, ARGS_SIMPLE>, 11
0007 opt_send_without_block                 <calldata!mid:initialize, argc:0, FCALL|ARGS_SIMPLE>
0009 jump                                   14
0011 opt_send_without_block                 <calldata!mid:new, argc:0, ARGS_SIMPLE>
0013 swap
0014 pop
0015 leave
```

This commit speeds up basic object allocation (`Foo.new`) by 60%, but classes that take keyword parameters see an even bigger benefit because no hash is allocated when instantiating the object (3x to 6x faster).

Here is an example that uses `Hash.new(capacity: 0)`:

```
> hyperfine "ruby --disable-gems -e'i = 0; while i < 10_000_000; Hash.new(capacity: 0); i += 1; end'" "./ruby --disable-gems -e'i = 0; while i < 10_000_000; Hash.new(capacity: 0); i += 1; end'"
Benchmark 1: ruby --disable-gems -e'i = 0; while i < 10_000_000; Hash.new(capacity: 0); i += 1; end'
  Time (mean ± σ):      1.082 s ±  0.004 s    [User: 1.074 s, System: 0.008 s]
  Range (min … max):    1.076 s …  1.088 s    10 runs

Benchmark 2: ./ruby --disable-gems -e'i = 0; while i < 10_000_000; Hash.new(capacity: 0); i += 1; end'
  Time (mean ± σ):     627.9 ms ±   3.5 ms    [User: 622.7 ms, System: 4.8 ms]
  Range (min … max):   622.7 ms … 633.2 ms    10 runs

Summary
  ./ruby --disable-gems -e'i = 0; while i < 10_000_000; Hash.new(capacity: 0); i += 1; end' ran
    1.72 ± 0.01 times faster than ruby --disable-gems -e'i = 0; while i < 10_000_000; Hash.new(capacity: 0); i += 1; end'
```

This commit changes the backtrace for `initialize`:

```
aaron@tc ~/g/ruby (inline-new)> cat test.rb
class Foo
  def initialize
    puts caller
  end
end

def hello
  Foo.new
end

hello
aaron@tc ~/g/ruby (inline-new)> ruby -v test.rb
ruby 3.4.2 (2025-02-15 revision d2930f8e7a) +PRISM [arm64-darwin24]
test.rb:8:in 'Class#new'
test.rb:8:in 'Object#hello'
test.rb:11:in '<main>'
aaron@tc ~/g/ruby (inline-new)> ./miniruby -v test.rb
ruby 3.5.0dev (2025-03-28T23:59:40Z inline-new c4157884e4) +PRISM [arm64-darwin24]
test.rb:8:in 'Object#hello'
test.rb:11:in '<main>'
```

It also increases memory usage for calls to `new` by 122 bytes:

```
aaron@tc ~/g/ruby (inline-new)> cat test.rb
require "objspace"

class Foo
  def initialize
    puts caller
  end
end

def hello
  Foo.new
end

puts ObjectSpace.memsize_of(RubyVM::InstructionSequence.of(method(:hello)))
aaron@tc ~/g/ruby (inline-new)> make runruby
RUBY_ON_BUG='gdb -x ./.gdbinit -p' ./miniruby -I./lib -I. -I.ext/common  ./tool/runruby.rb --extout=.ext  -- --disable-gems  ./test.rb
656
aaron@tc ~/g/ruby (inline-new)> ruby -v test.rb
ruby 3.4.2 (2025-02-15 revision d2930f8e7a) +PRISM [arm64-darwin24]
544
```

[Feature #21254](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/21254)

author: malfet
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #150780

To workaround limitation of 32-arguments per kernel and being able to eventually compile something like
```python
import torch

def foo(*args):
  rc = torch.empty_like(args[0])
  for arg in args:
      rc += arg
  return rc


tensors = torch.rand(100, 32, device='mps').unbind(0)
print(torch.compile(foo)(*tensors))
```

For now, introduce `at::native::metal::get_tensor_gpu_address` and use it from both C++ test and compile_shader to convert list of tensors to list of pointers valid on GPU.

Initially this binding were done via `id< MTLArgumentEncoder>`, but according to [Improving CPU Performance by Using Argument Buffers](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/improving-cpu-performance-by-using-argument-buffers?language=objc#Encode-Resources-into-Argument-Buffers) article, this is not necessary when targeting Tier2-only devices (which is true of all devices on MacOS-13 or newer):
> To directly encode the argument buffer resources on these Tier 2 devices, write the [MTLBuffer](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlbuffer?language=objc).[gpuAddress](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlbuffer/gpuaddress?language=objc) property — and for other resource types (samplers, textures, and acceleration structures), the [gpuResourceID](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlcomputepipelinestate/gpuresourceid?language=objc) property — into the corresponding structure member. To encode offsets, treat these property values as uint64 types and add the offset to them.

Add both C++ and PyThon unittests that validate that this works. 
Please note, that using either ArgumentEncoder or directly encoding the data does not guarantee buffer will not be freed until shader execution is complete. On the other hand, this should already be guaranteed by MPSCachingAllocator that would only free the memory after all streams completed its execution.

body:
## Description

This PR improves the `setup_appwrite.js` script to make the Appwrite project setup idempotent and more resilient. Previously, the script would fail with a database_already_exists error if the database was already created, even if it was empty or partially configured. This PR introduces logic to check for the existence of the database and collections before attempting to create them. It ensures that missing collections and attributes are added without affecting the existing setup.

Additional improvements include:

- Moved checkIns collection creation after users to maintain logical order.

- Added proper relationship checks between monuments and localExperts.

- Prevented duplicate collection creation by verifying existence before creation.

- Implemented retry mechanisms for attribute creation in case of delayed collection availability.

- Added error handling to gracefully manage already existing collections and attributes.

These changes allow the script to be safely re-run multiple times without requiring manual intervention, supporting a smoother and more robust setup experience.

Fixes #346

## Type of change

I have tested this with all possible permutations of database collection creation scenarios including:

- Creating all collections from scratch
- Creating collections when some already exist
- Creating monuments before localExperts and ensuring relationships are properly established
- Testing retry mechanisms for attribute setup with delayed collection availability
- Verifying proper handling of collections that already exist
- Confirming relationships between users and checkIns are correctly established
- Testing error handling when collections or attributes cannot be created
The solution now properly handles all edge cases and ensures idempotent creation of the database structure regardless of existing state.

author: jhiemstrawisc
body:
As #1808 states, we'd observed something strange in the relevant functions where a) the file URL generation function could return an empty URL without an associated error and b) that URL file could be successfully cleaned up, but logged in a way where the URL is empty. After closer inspection of these functions, my best bet is that we're running into a case where `url.Parse()` passes on an empty/invalid string and does not produce an error. As [docs for `url.Parse()`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url#Parse) indicate, the function may not always behave as expected due to "parsing ambiguities".

In addition to tidying up a few other error messages, I believe this makes it much harder for the conditions that caused this errant behavior to exist.

author: ericloe-cash
body:
The dynamo v2 API broke the way Dynamo Db Mapper would update the incoming item in memory when extensions updated it, such as version, timestamps, counters, etc.

To support this it requires an extension of our own to be installed on the `DynamoDbEnhancedClient`.
This extension relies on the fact the the enhanced client will create the real operation and apply extensions on the current thread before issuing the request that may be async.

The basic implementation is
- create a random UUID -> Tracker object in a global map
- set the current thread local to the UUID
- when the extension runs record the current item map on the Tracker mapped by the current threads UUID
- when the dynamo API returns read the latest item map from the global map

To support this the caller must
- Install the `WithResultExtension` on the EnhancedDynamoDbClient _last_
  - Mentions of this requirement are in as many relevant docs as possible.
  - Added to the migration guide how to do this.
- Use the OptIn `@WithResultExtensionInstalledLast` annotation when using saveWithResult methods to make it as visible as possible to install the extension _last_

body:
Create infrastructure to save user information. For now, the goal is to save the user preferences (eg. `{veg = True, halal = False, ...}`) as columns in a DB along with their netID. Then when they log in a later time to the site the preferences will auto-populate based on their last saved preferences. 

As of now, this PR only contains the backend for this database with a `database.py` that has three functions: `create_database`, `set_user_prefs`, and `get_user_prefs`. We still need to connect to the front end.

This pull request introduces a new feature to the Canvas Admin Tools extension, adding a "Sort Navigation" button to the course settings page. The button allows users to sort navigation items alphabetically and automatically save the changes. The most important changes include updates to the README documentation, the background script, and the addition of the new display script for sorting navigation items.

Background script updates:

* [`background/background.js`](diffhunk://#diff-c09a234d34a31a681bbf56b6a0170b2b9423138e4b34a7cee76e038ba2f5062fR86-R93): Added the `displaySortNavigation` script to the list of display scripts, specifying its details and the pages it will run on.

New display script:

author: jimrandomh
body:
The material-UI theming system has a concept of "overrides", where the theme contains styles identified by component name, that will be merged with a component's styles. We used this for some forum-gating (of both EA Forum and Alignment Forum styles) before we had a better idea of what our forum-gating mechanisms should be, but it's a bad mechanism because it makes it very easy to look at a component and overlook some styles it has.

Remove all overrides from our themes, for non-MUI components. (MUI components are removed from overrides separately, as they get typescriptified or removed.)

┆Issue is synchronized with this [Asana task](https://app.asana.com/0/1201302964208280/1209916575018759) by [Unito](https://www.unito.io)

<!--
Thank you for submitting a PR to pylint!

To ease the process of reviewing your PR, do make sure to complete the following boxes.

- [ ] Document your change, if it is a non-trivial one.
  - A maintainer might label the issue ``skip-news`` if the change does not need to be in the changelog.
  - Otherwise, create a news fragment with ``towncrier create <IssueNumber>.<type>`` which will be
    included in the changelog. ``<type>`` can be one of the types defined in `./towncrier.toml`.
    If necessary you can write details or offer examples on how the new change is supposed to work.
  - Generating the doc is done with ``tox -e docs``
- [ ] Relate your change to an issue in the tracker if such an issue exists (Refs #1234, Closes #1234)
- [ ] Write comprehensive commit messages and/or a good description of what the PR does.
- [ ] Keep the change small, separate the consensual changes from the opinionated one.
  Don't hesitate to open multiple PRs if the change requires it. If your review is so
  big it requires to actually plan and allocate time to review, it's more likely
  that it's going to go stale.
- [ ] If you used multiple emails or multiple names when contributing, add your mails
      and preferred name in ``script/.contributors_aliases.json``
-->

## Type of Changes

<!-- Leave the corresponding lines for the applicable type of change: -->

|     | Type                   |
| --- | ---------------------- |
| ✓   | :hammer: Refactoring   |

## Description

Follow up to #10288. Introducing dependency groups in` pyproject.toml` and cleaning up the file a little bit. Once pip fully supports PEP735, we should update the documentation and remove all the `requirement.txt` files.

With this change you are able to install dependencies like this:

```bash
uv pip install -e . --group docs # installs docs requirements
uv pip install -e .[spelling] --group docs --group dev # installs pre-commit and docs requirements + spelling extras
```

One thing I am currently unsure is how the dependencies in `.readthedocs.yaml` would be handled, when the requirement files in the doc folder are removed?

author: dadrus
body:
This PR updates the default main port to 4456, reverting to the value used for the decision service prior to #2089. Although the referenced PR introduces a breaking change, this adjustment reduces its impact on setups running heimdall in decision operation mode, which appears to be the most common use case across projects. For those using heimdall in proxy mode, the desired port can be set via the available configuration option, as shown below. 

```yaml
# heimdall config file
serve:
  port: 4455
```

If a Helm chart is used for deployment in proxy mode, the previous behavior - using port 4455 for the exposed service - can be restored, as also demonstrated below.

```yaml
# your helm chart value file

service:
  main:
    port: 4455
```

body:
I made changes that expands the addon's capabilities in this areas:

- Material Conversion: Automatic PRM texture generation from Principled BSDF
  with customizable resolution (64-8192px) and fallback methods

- Animation Tools: Complete IK rigging system with pose library, hip 
  animation transfer, and specialized IK controls for arms/legs.

- Model and Animation import improvements: Now you can select a mod folder that will show a list in the UI of all your movesets 
   or skins for you to easily import. If the plugin finds that the model has a related animation folder, it will make a list of all the 
   animation available in the animation import section. It also has the hability to import a folder of your liking. The new features 
   dont replace the original ones, you can still import a standalone model or animation.

- Exo Management: New ability to "un-exo" models with bone cleanup,
  weight transfer, and improved hierarchy management

- UI Improvements: Enhanced panels, better error reporting, and
  resource-aware processing for texture generation

- Swing QOL feature: Added a option to copy swing bones values or collisions between bones.

This update is mainly focused on improving animation workflow but it has some extra enhancements in other areas.

body:
This PR changes the Vertex AI eval clients to pass necessary info from EvalClient init arguments instead of environment variables so that we can easily use Vertex AI client and non Vertex AI client.
This also bumps the version to `0.10.0.dev3`.

```python
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

from langcheck.metrics.eval_clients import (
    AnthropicEvalClient,
    GeminiEvalClient,
)

# The following environment variables should be set
# ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID=<your-project-id>
# CLOUD_ML_REGION=<region>  (e.g. europe-west1)
# GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=<path-to-credentials-file>
anthropic_client = AnthropicEvalClient(vertexai=True)

# The following environment variables should be set
# GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=<your-project-id>
# GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=<location>  (e.g. europe-west1)
# GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=<path-to-credentials-file>
gemini_client = GeminiEvalClient(
    model_name="gemini-2.0-flash",
    embed_model_name="text-embedding-004",
    vertexai=True
)

anthropic_response = anthropic_client.get_text_responses(
    prompts=["Hello"]
)
gemini_response = gemini_client.get_text_responses(
    prompts=["Hello"]
)

```

## Summary
This PR implements a dual enhancement: (1) improved task management with proper status handling for stopped workflows, and (2) significant UI updates including collapsible panels, categorized task displays, and enhanced visual feedback throughout the application.

## Changes

### Task Status Handling
- Added a new `stopped` status to task types
- Modified workflow termination to use the stopped status instead of immediately failing tasks
- Improved task completion logic to handle stopped tasks appropriately

### UI Improvements
- Added collapsible logs panel with smooth transitions
- Separated task display into scheduled/processing/completed categories
- Improved visual feedback for stopped tasks in the input area
- Added expand/collapse controls with neural node styling
- Set metadata components to be expanded by default
- Enhanced ScheduleBox with UI elements to display different task categories
- Implemented separate streams for scheduled, processing, and completed tasks

### Backend Improvements
- Enhanced task queue management to properly track stopped tasks
- Updated DB controller to handle the new stopped status
- Modified orchestrator workflow to gracefully handle task stopping

Closes #342, #386

```
+ pgmq                   | pgmq                     | drop_queue                                       | queue_name text, partitioned boolean                                              >
```

body:
# Why

Keeping logical grouping for memory ids might have people be tempted to define the ids non-consecutively, which can lead to bugs where memory ids are reused. Having logical grouping isn't that beneficial for defining ids, since the logical relationship between the memories can still be seen where they are used.

# What

* Keep memory ids sorted
* Remove logical grouping

author: lifeofhacks
body:
## Overview
This PR implements a set of Clarity smart contracts for tokenized equipment maintenance on the Stacks blockchain. The system enables industrial equipment registration, service agreement management, performance tracking, and automated payments based on equipment performance.

## Contracts

### 1. Asset Registration Contract
- Implements NFT-based equipment registration
- Stores detailed equipment information
- Enables ownership transfer and location updates
- Provides read-only functions to query equipment details

### 2. Service Agreement Contract
- Creates maintenance agreements between equipment owners and service providers
- Schedules maintenance based on defined intervals
- Tracks completion of maintenance tasks
- Allows agreement termination

### 3. Performance Tracking Contract
- Monitors equipment uptime and downtime
- Tracks equipment operational status
- Records and resolves equipment issues
- Calculates reliability metrics

### 4. Payment Automation Contract
- Calculates payment amounts based on performance metrics
- Implements escrow for service payments
- Processes payments for completed maintenance
- Handles payment disputes

## Testing
- Comprehensive test suite using Vitest
- Tests cover all major contract functions
- Mocks used to simulate contract interactions

## Implementation Notes
- All contracts use Clarity's built-in data structures and functions
- NFTs used for equipment and agreement representation
- Performance-based payment adjustments incentivize quality service
- Escrow system ensures fair payment processing
